name: 420Search
purpose: Unified discovery across public 420 Integrated chain state, registered protocol services, application-owned records and explicitly indexable ecosystem content.

canonicalSources.commons: 420 Commons public/indexable spaces and metadata only
canonicalSources.pulse: 420 Pulse public/indexable publications and topics only
canonicalSources.otherProtocols: protocol-owned public events and reads discovered through 420Registry

invariants: SRCH-INV-001: 420Search owns no canonical protocol state and requires no Search-specific Genesis contract.
SRCH-INV-002: Every result identifies or preserves the authority of its underlying source; a search index cannot overwrite canonical chain or protocol state.
SRCH-INV-003: Search ranking, relevance scores, snippets, labels, categories and recommendations are non-canonical presentation metadata.
SRCH-INV-004: Sponsored placement is explicitly labeled and cannot alter canonical ownership, identity, rights, listing, payment, trust or protocol fields.
SRCH-INV-005: On-chain results remain traceable to chain ID and canonical block/transaction/log references; finalized history is not silently rewritten.
SRCH-INV-006: The complete public search index can be rebuilt from supported canonical sources without trusting a hosted Search database.
SRCH-INV-007: Private or encrypted Messenger, Commons and Resource Protocol payloads, private Identity data and raw Attention telemetry are excluded from the index.
SRCH-INV-008: A visible hash, commitment or ciphertext reference does not grant Search operators permission to retrieve, decrypt or infer protected payloads.
SRCH-INV-009: Search operators gain no custody, smart-account execution, governance, validator, bridge or token-transfer authority.
SRCH-INV-010: Search unavailability cannot block direct wallet, Explorer, RPC, contract or protocol interaction.
SRCH-INV-011: Public Search APIs expose index freshness, chain/network identity and source provenance so clients can detect stale or wrong-network results.
SRCH-INV-012: Pagination and result identifiers are stable for a fixed index snapshot, enabling reproducible clients and auditable result retrieval.
